content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper combines Bayesian neural networks and hypernetworks to extend ideas first presented by model-agnostic meta-learning.  Instead of gradient-based updates to the universal parameters in the adaptation phase, the hypernetwork provides an update to the universal parameters as a function of the query set.  The model performs broadly in line with other methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
# Strengths
The idea of using a hypernetwork to predict the update to a BNN is sound enough.  It does have appealing benefits compared to the MAML-style gradient updates.  Parameterizing the parameter distribution directly also seems novel.  

# Weaknesses
I have three main complaints.  Foremost, the presentation of the method is cluttered and confusing.  The paper itself is also well below the required threshold.  Finally, the method doesn’t appear to perform especially well empirically.  

## Presentation of the method
I think the idea of the method is sound enough – use a hypernetwork to predict the update to universal parameters in a Bayesian neural network.  I wish the authors had stripped away all the “fat” in the paper and really focussed on presenting this.  All the other stuff is actually confusing to the reader and gets in the way of the core message.  We only get to the method at the bottom of page five, and is finished midway down page six.  This suggests that there is too much material above.  

There are also fairly fundamental aspects of the method that are unclear:  how is the support set aggregated by $f_{\theta}$ (which is defined previously as a classifier…) to produce the updates?  How is the proposal parameterised?  What are $\lambda$ and $\psi$?  How does the hypernetwork work, as taking $S$ and $f_{\theta}(S)$ as inputs is not clear to me?  The spaces of many of the functions, parameters and variables are undefined, and it seems that some of the terminology is overloaded.  What is the role of the proposal in the final network?  Figure 2 doesn't have a proposal in it?  How is the query set used in the final blue box?  Shouldn't that be a Q?  

## Presentation of the paper
The paper more generally is poorly presented.  It is littered with spelling errors and typographical mistakes which make it difficult to read and causes confusion over what is actually being described / implemented.  There are also numerous unsubstantiated claims throughout the paper: “Bayesian treatment **prevents** overfitting”, “allows larger updates”, “scales better” etc.  The exploratory experiment in Figure 3 is also basically unexplained, and Figure 2 need to be improved and expanded upon, because it currently doesn’t seem to actually match the architecture ($\theta$ is sampled, but then $\mu(S)$ is then also used in the next box?).

There also seems to be an inconsistency in the definitions of support and query sets.  You say that M is typically larger than K, but this is not as imaged in Figure 2.  It is also my understanding that typically the support set has many examples, and the query set has just a few examples.  But I may be wrong.  

## Empirical performance
Although being SotA certainly isn’t required for publication, the empirical results are not especially compelling and do not back up the claims made in the main text.  BayesHMAML+adaptation generally outperforms BayesHMAML, suggesting that adaptation steps are still required and that a hypernetwork alone isn’t sufficient (as is implied in the main text).  Other methods still outperform both these methods, and so it is unclear (at best…) as to whether Bayesian approaches have helped.  I would also like to see the method benchmarked on a few more datasets.  Finally, the exploratory experiment in Figure 3 needs much more explanation and digging in to.  I say this because it was my understanding that BNNs do not **solve** uncertainty estimation, and so there may be further opportunities to explore this result and the calibration of the learned models. 


# Minor Weaknesses / Typographical Mistakes

(a)  The abstract is too long.

(b)  \citep and \citet are used incorrectly.  

(c)  KL typically has a double pipe, i.e. $KL(\cdot || \cdot)$.

(d)  Please number your equations.

(e)  We can probably remove some rows of the table in the main, and include a full table in the supplement.

(f)  What is the y-axis on Figure 3?

(g)  Some typos:   “Analogically”, “reprehension”, “Such the”, “is corresponding”

(h)  Only proper nouns should be capitalised, eg. “Few-Shot” -> “few-shot”.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The work appears novel and original, although it is a combination of existing ideas.  The presentation of the material is well-below par.  I believe the work to be somewhat reproducible, as I “believe” the results, but the paper alone would be insufficient to reproduce the results (although the authors did promise code after review).
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I think the core idea is reasonably sound.  Unfortunately, the paper is no way near ready for publication yet.  The low quality of the manuscript actively prevents me from thoroughly evaluating the method.  I think there could be a conference paper in this line of work in the future, but it is not currently at that point.  I encourage the authors to rework the presentation of the method and expand the empirical validation. Good luck.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
- This paper illustrates Bayesian variants of MAML (BH-MAML) for few-shot learning.
- Specifically, a hypernetwork is used to predict $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$ of adaptation process of global initialization.
- Then the adapted weight is summation of global initialization and adaptation sampled from $N(\mu, \sigma^2)$.
- The meta loss is the average of cross entropy loss over meta mini-batch, where the adaptation is regularized by KL div between standard normal distribtution.
- The experiments show the effectiveness of the proposed methods in comparison to relevant baselines.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. This paper provides a clear motivation and its explanation via the concept figure 1.
2. The experimental results is somewhat strong in comparison to BayesianMAML and HyperMAML.

Weakness:
1. The "novelty" of this paper is somewhat controversial. There are two positions for this paper: 1) Hypernetwork-approach for meta-learning and 2) Bayesian MAML approach. In the perspective of 1), this paper is very similar to HyperMAML (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.15745.pdf), and the technical difference is that this paper learns variance of adaptation. In comparison to Bayesian approaches, BH-MAML is very similar to VERSA (https://openreview.net/pdf?id=HkxStoC5F7), and the major difference BH-MAML learns global initialization. This should be discussed in depth.
2. This paper is not "self-contained". I can't find any details of hypernetwork ($H_\phi(S)$ in Figure 2). The hypernetwork is main technical novelty of this paper, so it should be explained in this paper (the hypernetwork might be the one from HyperMAML). 
3. As far as I know, any Bayesian methods suffer from computational overhead since they randomly sample weights from distribution and take a average of the sampled weights (e.g., Monte Carlo). Does BH-MAML suffer from same problem? If so, is the overhead negligible or not? How many samples are used for estimation? These questions are not discussed in the paper.
4. The most relevant baseline for BH-MAML is not MAML but ANIL (https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.09157) since BH-MAML does not update the feature extractor in the inner loop. ANIL is missing in the paper (both related work and experiments section).
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: This paper is clearly written with a motivating plot: see strengths 1.

Quality: This paper is not ``self-contained'': see weakness 2, 3 and 4.

Novelty: This paper is somewhat not ``novel'': see weakness 1,  but I am willing to change my score in this respect.

Reproducibility: This paper does not provide the Hypernetwork architecture in details: see weakness 2.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposes a motivating Bayesian framework based on MAML, where the task adaptation through gradient descent are amortized by Hypernetwork. The main concern is that this paper is not "self-contained".
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new approach of Bayesian meta-learning, which is based on MAML and Hypernetworks. In particular, the hypernetworks are adopted to directly produces posterior distributions of weights for few-shot tasks by aggregating information from support sets and common universal weights.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
(-) The benefits from the properties of Bayesian framework are not well shown. Compared to other Bayesian meta-learning approaches, this work lacks related experiments.  Also, the related results in Figure 3 are unclear to understand the context in Section 5.3
(-) The proposed method is a hybrid approach that is based on optimization-based and model-based methods. That way, the method should be compared with some model-based methods rather than MAML-based methods.
(-) It is unclear that the proposed method is really model-agnostic, although the authors claim that the model is based on MAML.
(-) The method is quite similar to LEO (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1807.05960.pdf), but the authors never mentioned about it. LEO works in the embedding space instead of the parameter space, which this method uses.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The objective function does not included the parameters $\phi$ related to the hypernetwork, and it is unclear to understand the relationship between $\lambda$ and $H_{\phi}$.
- It is unclear how the hypernetwork processes the support set. Is it order invariant? HyperMAML should be first explained in details to properly understand the overall approach.
- The proposed method lacks technical novelty as it simply extended HyperMAML by additionally predicting the variance term.
content.summary_of_the_review:
- The proposed method lacks technical novelty as it simply extended HyperMAML by additionally predicting the variance term.  
- The benefits from the properties of Bayesian framework are not well shown, and the overall performance is not impressive as well.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
